messages:
Anya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to add a lightweight translation facade between control plane and runtime so Hosted/Dedicated/Private can negotiate capabilities without full schema duplication.
Sam: Sketch?
Anya: Idea: each deployment exposes a small /capabilities RPC that returns a stable capability-set and a version. Runtime then maps API verbs onto supported primitives. Keeps host-level API stable.
Jin: That sounds like capability negotiation. How do we handle auth differences? Private customers often want customer-managed tokens and no control-plane secret passing.
Todd: We should separate control-plane metadata from data-plane auth. Control-plane can get capabilities and routing hints. Data-plane auth is always direct from client to runtime (signed token exchange). No secrets proxied.
Sam: OK but we still need a mechanism for the Console and Optimize to query metrics and logs across modes. Private deployments may want logs to stay local.
Anya: Two parts: 1) Observability API surface (read-only, coarse metrics) that can be optionally federated; 2) A mandatory heartbeat + minimal traces API for SLA checks (only status, latency p50/p95). Private can opt-out but then SLA flows are different.
Jin: Failure modes: what happens when a hosted-only feature (e.g., experimental KV-cache prefetch) is requested by an app pinned to private?
Todd: Runtime should return a 501 with capability mismatch details. Client SDKs will translate into fallback policies: degrade to non-prefetching path or route to compatible variant (if allowed by tenant policy).
Anya: We need a compact error contract: {"code":"CAP_MISMATCH","capability":"kv_prefetch","required_version":"2"}. Keep messages machine-parsable.
Sam: Could we add a negotiation header so proxies can preflight and pick an allowed variant? e.g., `X-Redwood-Expect-Cap: kv_prefetch/v2`
Jin: Headers for negotiation are OK but must be idempotent and cheap. Also need to avoid leaking customer capability choices in hosted logs. Mark header as sensitive.
ops-bot: deploy-check:cap-facade v0.1 passed on staging -> canary rollout tomorrow at 03:00 UTC :white_check_mark:
Todd: Rollout note — facade must be backward compatible for 6 months. Any new capability IDs must be additive.
Anya: Testing plan: unit harness for capability map translation + integration test that simulates 3 runtime profiles (hosted-full, dedicated-lite, private-min). Add a fuzz test that randomizes missing capabilities to ensure graceful fallback.
Sam: Ops question: Who owns the translation tables? infra-runtime or product?
Anya: Short answer: infra-runtime owns runtime mapping; product owns public capability catalog and deprecation timeline. We maintain a single source-of-truth YAML in repo, with a changelog PR process.
Jin: How to handle rollbacks when a capability causes performance regression in dedicated?
Todd: Add runtime flags for 'capability soft-enable' where capability starts in observation-only mode (metrics emitted but not used) then opt-in toggle per pool. Allows quick rollback.
Sam: Nice. Also need a simple doc for customers: "capabilities and fallbacks". I'll draft after canary.
Anya: Action items: 1) Todd to add /capabilities contract spec + error contract. 2) Jin to design auth separation doc. 3) Sam to update onboarding docs and SDK header behavior. 4) Ops to schedule canary.
ops-bot: created issue RW-4123: implement-capability-facade (link)
Anya: Thanks — keeping this small and explicit reduces long-term adapter sprawl. We'll reconvene after canary results.
Sam: :thumbsup:
